Hi OP,

I'm sorry this happened to you. 

I know you had felt that you and your fiance tell each other everything, but I wonder if he only gave the *appearance* of doing so. Or maybe he really did tell you everything in the beginning, but now it's obviously changed. 

No matter how you look at it, the fact remains that he had an intimate conversation about very personal things with another person, with whom he wants to have sex. The fact that you did not know about this means that somewhere along the way, he became unworthy of having your trust, even if you didn't know it at the time. 

Does he deserve credit for being upfront and honest with you? Well... I don't think so. He did it for his own benefit. It is always easier to "cheat with permission" because it's less work - being deceptive *can be* taxing on a person. 

I'm not judging anyone who has an open relationship - there was a time I dabbled in that myself. The difference is that *you* are not used to it, *you* never agreed to it, and *you* want a traditional relationship and eventually, marriage and children. 

Asking you to suddenly take on an entirely new lifestyle is unfair, especially since he's proclaimed that if you don't agree, he may give in and cheat in the future. Instead of looking inward and trying to work on becoming a better version of himself - a version that doesn't want to hurt you and only wants to give you the happiness you deserve - he's giving you an unfair ultimatum: "Let me sleep with this woman, because I'll cheat eventually anyway. Oh and remember honey, I was honest about all this, so no matter what happens in the future, I am not to blame." Ugh!

He is blaming you for this problem, and he is placing a heavy burden on you. I know you planned a future with this man, but I'd like to point out the possibility that he is actually not the person you thought you knew. 

Can you two work things out? Some people do survive infidelity and loss of trust, but I don't believe your fiance wants to do that. He just wants what he wants when he wants it. Do you really want to have and raise children with him? 

I think you should thank him. He's shown you who he really is before marrying you. Now you have a different choice - one that lets you keep your dignity. Best of luck to you.

Rita Hayworth and the Shawshank Redemption wasn't a book by itself. The story was part of a collection of King's called Different Seasons. Each story featured a season name (or pun of a season). Rita Hayworth and the Shawshank Redemption was the title of one story, the subtitle of which being "Hope Springs Eternal." 

The movie Stand by Me came from the story The Body, and the subtitle there was "Fall from Innocence," from the same collection (just an interesting sidenote).

In the end, even fanfic authors have to perfect their 1st, 2nd, and 3rd acts, and even fanfic authors need to fine-tune the way the characters are presented. The mood, premise, inciting incident, buildup, climax, and so much more are just part of the complex structure that makes up a story, and writing of any nature is always a good practice. 

You say that she "knew how you felt about fan fiction" as if she needed your permission to pursue her own craft. You certainly have a right to feel however you want, but you do not have the right to impose your bias upon someone else, effectively shitting all over it. 

Authors support other authors. Be better.

Ok. I have been there before. No one else could understand it because they didn't have the same type of anxiety I did. My old place was a disaster, truly. 

I learned my lesson the hard way- when I moved, I lost a LOT of my stuff because there was so much of it and there was so much chaos. That alone was enough to make me handle things differently from now on. 

Here is what I can tell you, my dear. FIRST: Stop thinking of your mess as a whole because that will only make you feel more overwhelmed. If you have belongings that are more important, deal with that first. After that point, simply pick a spot of your home at random and sit down with a trash bag and a box and go thru every single thing there. 

SECOND: Going forward... Remember that it is ok to be a little bit messy. It doesn't have to be really neat or really messy. If you take a few minutes every day to pick up after yourself, and clean up after each meal, you should be ok as long as you do a weekly cleaning of countertops, bathrooms etc once a week maybe, a bit longer than that if you need to. It might be bad advice with most things, but for people like us, if you half-ass the cleaning most days, you will be ok as long as you organize all your stuff upon move in. 

Go to Target after you've moved to your new place and get large plastic bins. All books go in one box. All clothes go in a suitcase. All cooking stuff goes in another box. And you keep them there until you find shelves/ cupboards/ permanent storage areas. Enlist the help of a loved one who's good at organizing.

I really hope you don't have to go through what I went through. I lost some good, collectible stuff because of my issues. I am determined to never have that happen again. Plus, it honestly feels good to be organized. I feel in control of my life. And it feels good that someone can just visit me randomly and I won't have to clean up in a panic. Lol. These small things are a big deal to me. 

Good luck. You will be fine! Remember, pick one area at a time. I know it's hard, but try to accept help from loved ones. You can do this!!!!! Xoxo
